title: Sierra Retail - incident scratch notes
content:
Quick scratchpad for Sierra Retail incident (private VPC). Notes to self + draft comms.

Summary:
- Started 2025-02-14 03:12 UTC: customer reports surge in 5xx/latency for hosted endpoint mapped to their private deployment (vpc-prod-1).
- Observable: steady increase in tail latency, periodic 503s and grpc Unavailable errors from router to runtime. No change in request rate per LB metrics.
- Impact: intermittent failures for up to 20% of requests to /v1/generate with sequences >1024 tokens.

Commands run / quick outputs (kept raw):
1) kubectl -n redwood-runtime get pods -l app=runtime -o wide\   (checked node placement)
-> runtime-0  Ready 1/1  4d   10.240.8.32  us-central1-a  0.2% CPU
-> runtime-1  CrashLoopBackOff  0/1  1h  10.240.8.35  us-central1-b\n\n2) kubectl -n redwood-runtime logs runtime-1 --since=30m | tail -n 80\-> [2025-02-14T02:46:12Z] WARN kv_cache: miss_rate=0.91 prefix_hits=0.03\-> [2025-02-14T02:46:14Z] ERROR infer: batch_exec failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed\-> panic: runtime: out of memory

3) top on node-12 (gce) at 02:50 UTC:\-> processes: redwood-runtime (pid 4321) VIRT=18G RES=14.8G  -> mem near saturation (94%)

4) curl -v "https://private-api.sierra.redwood/v1/health" --resolve private-api.sierra.redwood:443:10.240.9.10\-> * Connected to private-api.sierra.redwood (10.240.9.10)\-> < HTTP/1.1 200 OK\-> {"status":"ok","runtime_version":"v1.12.3"}

5) grpc probe to runtime-1: (using grpcurl)\-> Error: UNAVAILABLE: connection closed before message completed

Notable error snippets copied:
- "kv_cache miss_rate=0.91 prefix_hits=0.03; evicting 82 entries /s"
- "batch_exec failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed"
- "runtime: out of memory"
- "channel: send failed: broken pipe"

Timeline (from logs + customer):
- 2025-02-13 23:30 UTC: Customer started large batch job (downstream indexing) - ~1.5x normal tokens/s, heavy long context usage (configured max_seq_len 2048)
- 2025-02-14 01:08 UTC: First spike in KV cache evictions observed (evict rate jumps 8x)
- 2025-02-14 02:15 UTC: runtime-1 OOM and restarted (CrashLoopBackOff)
- 2025-02-14 03:12 UTC: Customer reported increased 5xx, ticket SR-1789 opened
- 2025-02-14 04:00 UTC: Temporarily scaled up node pool (added node-13), moved some pods -> partial relief, but tail latency still high

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV cache thrashing due to sudden change in workload (long sequences + high cardinality prefixes) causes memory pressure and OOM on some runtime replicas leading to grpc failures.
2) A model change (they pinned model:v1.12.3) introduced a regression in memory kernel for long context (unlikely but check recent rollout).
3) Underprovisioned instance type for this workload when sequence lengths >1024 causing resource exhaustion during peak batched execution.
4) Network flakiness between router and runtime causing grpc channels to die under load (less likely given OOM traces).

Quick actions taken / in flight:
- Rolled runtime-1 to debug image with additional heap profiling flags (started at 04:10 UTC) -> collecting /debug/heap at /tmp/heap-04-20.pb
- Increased eviction aggressiveness: kv_cache.capacity -> -20% (temporary) on node-13 pool via configmap -> applied 04:35 UTC
- Opened debug SSH to node-12, pulled core dump, saved to gs://redwood-debug/sierra/2025-02-14/core-runtime-1-02:40.gz
- Repeated small-scale load test against private endpoint (seq_len=1536, batch=4) -> reproduced increased latency and occasional 503s

Observations after tweaks:
- eviction rate down to 0.65 miss_rate (was 0.91) -> reduced memory pressure but not eliminated
- runtime-1 still restarted twice in 3h window (new crashes show similar OOM stack)

Stack traces (relevant lines):
- goroutine 412 [running]:
  runtime.throw(0x4f5a2c, 0x16)
  runtime: out of memory
- infer/batcher.go:142  batchExec() -> allocation of 12.3GB for kv-shard

Immediate next steps (priority):
- 1) Ask customer to pause the downstream indexing job (non-urgent but high impact) for 1 hour to see baseline -> contacting via solutions PM now.
- 2) Temporarily reduce max_seq_len in their deployment to 1024 (config override) as quick mitigation.
- 3) Keep collecting heap profiles and enable jemalloc stats on the debug pod.
- 4) Run targeted unit test reproducer for kv-cache with high cardinality prefixes locally (Ethan assigned).
- 5) Prepare rollback of any recent runtime image if model kernel suspected.

Draft internal blurb for ENG-SRE (short):
---
Oncall/ENG-SRE,
Sierra Retail (SR-1789) is seeing periodic 5xx and high tail latency on their private runtime. Root cause suspected: KV cache thrashing leading to OOMs on some runtime replicas under long-context workload. We've applied temporary eviction and scaled nodes; still seeing restarts. Collecting heap profiles and core dumps (gs://redwood-debug/sierra/...). Please prioritize: repro path + memory allocation tracing on runtime.
---

Draft customer-facing note (to be reviewed by PM/legal):
Subject: Brief update on incident impacting your private deployment
Hi Team Sierra,
We are actively investigating the increased latency and intermittent errors you reported. Initial findings indicate memory pressure on a subset of runtime replicas driven by long-sequence requests that caused KV cache evictions and, in some cases, process restarts.
Actions taken so far:
- Added temporary capacity and adjusted cache eviction thresholds to reduce memory pressure.
- Collecting heap profiles and core dumps for deeper analysis.
- Suggested short-term mitigation: pause the heavy indexing job or reduce max sequence length to 1024 for the next 60–90 minutes.
Next steps:
- We'll share a targeted mitigation plan within 2 hours and aim to have a more permanent configuration/patch within 24–48 hours.
Thanks for your patience — we know this is disruptive.
Maya (Solutions Eng)

Notes to self:
- Check if SR-1743 (last week) had a similar pattern (kv eviction spikes) -> possible regression in evict heuristics.
- If we can reproduce consistently, add a Canary test that simulates 1.5x tokens/s with seq_len=1536 in CI.
- Keep this doc as the working timeline for postmortem; move to shared drive when stable.

Unresolved questions:
- Why only node-1 replica shows OOM while others survive same traffic? (Check node labels, NUMA config, different kernel/jemalloc versions)
- Did customer change any client-side batching recently? (PM to confirm)

End of scratch notes.
